sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bonn's parking policy has aimed to move cars off the street and into garages. Since 1 June 2022 on-street parking in the centre has cost €4 an hour, with €3 in Beuel and Bad Godesberg and €2 in Hardtberg, while garage prices were left unchanged. A Green councillor said the aim was to move parking into garages [0]. Resident parking has since spread. A Nordstadt concept was due to start on 4 November 2024, with most public spaces reserved for permit holders and everyone else buying a ticket, Monday to Saturday from 8:00 to 22:00 [3], and the city planned to introduce management in Beuel-Zentrum from 2026 [4]. Bonn has also tried reserving business parking spaces for tradespeople and delivery vehicles in Südstadt and Kessenich [5], and a one-year pilot opened a retail car park to neighbours in the evening [6].

The resident permit became expensive and is now being cut back. The council raised it to €180 a year from March 2023 and €360 from March 2024. After a Cologne court found the ordinance lacked a clause on who owes the fee, a corrected version was approved retroactively, without objection to the amounts [1][2]. In March 2026 the council approved lower fees of €120 for one year and €240 for two, with formal adoption scheduled for May 2026 [1]. We have not confirmed that adoption.

Access to the centre has recently been squeezed by the bridge. The A565 Nordbrücke, which carries about 100,000 vehicles a day, has been fully closed since 3 June 2026. Bonn expanded park-and-ride and bus links [10], reportedly made public transport free from 15 to 30 June [11], and decided on 15 June to develop a 200-space park-and-ride site at Vilich [12]. Earlier, in September 2024, local business groups complained of long queues at the exits of the Markt and Uni garages and asked for the Cityring to be opened for garage traffic [9].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Bonn's central supply is mostly garages run by one company, Bonner City Parkraum (BCP), which lists eleven facilities [14]. It has spent the last years refurbishing them. The Unigarage reopened in April 2020 after refurbishment, the new Parkhaus Hauptbahnhof opened in May 2020 and the Alte Bahnhofgarage reopened in November 2020 [20]. The Friedensplatzgarage, the largest, was refurbished in live operation from August 2023 and the work was reported complete in November 2024 [19]. In December 2025 BCP put the 58-space Beethoven-Parkplatz back into operation just before the Beethovenhalle reopened [17]. In 2023 business groups asked politicians to discuss city-centre parking, and Haus & Grund warned that rejecting a new underground garage at the Viktoriakarree would risk forfeiting a chance to improve it. That was a lobby position, not a council decision [25].

Technology has been added across the garages. Since April 2025 customers at all BCP garages can pay by smartphone against their licence plate [16], and from November 2025 the Operngarage machines preselect a €5 event tariff on opera days to speed exits [18]. SWB, the Stadtwerke Bonn subsidiary, reported reaching 640 public charging points in Bonn, mainly on city parking areas, with some in BCP garages [22]. BCP's managing director said garages fill from November to January and are sometimes nearly full when Black Friday and the Christmas market coincide, with the Marktgarage filling first [21]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Bonn data cover 21 garages with 5,280 spaces. Eight lie within 500 m of the Markt (2,831 spaces) and five more within 1 km (1,015). BCP dominates: eleven garages with 3,560 spaces, 94% of them within 1 km, nine of them at one published tariff of €2.00 an hour for the first two hours, €2.50 afterwards, €25 a day on weekdays and €8 on Sundays and holidays [15]. Beyond BCP the centre has few competitors: APCOA's 97-space City Garage Bonn at €1.99 an hour, Contipark's Brückenforum garage 1.0 km out at €1.20, and further away B+B's 535-space Museumsmeile garage (2.8 km) and Q-Park's Fronhofer Galeria (272 spaces, 6.8 km, €2.50). DB BahnPark's four other car parks are around 7 km out.

BCP's occupancy feed covers nine garages with 3,362 spaces. They averaged 34% on weekdays and 34% at weekends from August to early October 2026, so these garages are as full at weekends as on weekdays. The fullest is a 94-space station garage (66% on weekdays and weekends), followed by Rabinstraße (305 spaces, 49%) and, among the central garages, the Marktgarage (42%), Unigarage (38%) and Stadthaus (37%). The Friedensplatzgarage (810 spaces) is 33% full, the Münsterplatz garage 20% and the Operngarage 15%. The BCP garages share a tariff, so price does not explain differences among them.

The feed's station garages do not match BCP's listings by name or capacity, so we do not pair them. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ. In the nine garages with data in both years, occupancy averaged 33% in 2022 and 41% in 2025.
